name: Sir Abubakar Tafawa Balewa
summary: First and only Prime Minister of Nigeria (1957-66). A former teacher who helped found the Northern People's Congress, he spoke for Northern interests in the 1940s and 1950s legislatures, led a coalition government after independence, and helped found the Organization of African Unity in 1963. Killed in the January 1966 coup.
notes: DOCUMENTED: identity -55. In the Legislative Council he said Nigerian unity was only a British intention and that Northerners saw Southern settlers as 'invaders' (source dates it 1947; other sites say 1948 or 1949). https://www.vanguardngr.com/2022/10/the-2023-presidential-election-and-the-national-question/ (opened; an opinion column quoting Hansard). Period: 1947-52. DOCUMENTED MIX: global 0. His 1963 OAU speech warned against economic domination, but his foreign policy was anti-communist and pro-Western (https://www.nationalrecord.com.ng/africa-day-2026-nigeria-has-obligations-to-africans-by-owei-lakemfa/ , opened). ESTIMATED from overall record: economy +15 (search excerpts described him as a pro-British conservative with a pro-Western foreign policy; those source pages were not retained), federalism +45 (spoke for Northern regional interests, led a regionally based coalition), power -30 (regionally balanced cabinets), security -20, social -20 (conservative label), democracy +30 (parliamentary government 1957-66). ZERO-PLACEHOLDER: religion, corruption.

name: Chief Anthony Enahoro
summary: Journalist and Action Group politician who moved the 1953 motion for Nigerian self-government in 1956. He demanded a Benin-Delta State from 1951 and served as a federal commissioner under General Gowon (1967-74). In the 1990s he helped found the Movement for National Reformation and NADECO, led NADECO from 1997, and was detained for four months in 1994.
notes: DOCUMENTED (one opened page: https://blerf.org/index.php/biography/enahoro-chief-anthony/ , a compiled biography): federalism +80 (demanded a Benin-Delta State in 1951-53; co-founded the Movement for National Reformation, launched 5 December 1992, to restore true federalism; urged devolution from an all-powerful centre); democracy +70 (denounced military rule, protested the June 1993 annulment, co-founded NADECO in 1994, led it from 1997, detained 1994). Period: 1990s. ESTIMATED: economy -35 (served as deputy of the Action Group, whose official ideology was democratic socialism), identity +35 (moved the all-Nigeria independence motion and served the federal side in the civil war, but also pressed a regional state demand), power -30 (power-sharing and national-conference advocate), global -10 (anti-colonial nationalist). ZERO-PLACEHOLDER: religion, security, social, corruption.

name: Margaret Ekpo
summary: Women's rights activist and politician from Aba. She organised the Aba Market Women Association and the Aba Township Women's Association, led the NCNC women's wing, was nominated to the Eastern House of Chiefs, and won a seat in the Eastern Regional House of Assembly in 1961.
notes: DOCUMENTED (opened https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaret_Ekpo ): social +45. From the late 1940s she organised market women to press for women's economic protections and political rights and demanded for Nigerian women the civil rights women abroad were winning. Covers gender issues only. ESTIMATED: economy +20 (built trader associations around economic protections for market women, not state ownership), identity +35 (the page says she was among women activists who rallied women beyond ethnic solidarity, a group description), democracy +45 (campaigned to widen political participation and won a seat in 1961). ZERO-PLACEHOLDER: federalism, religion, power, security, global, corruption. Sources disagree on the House of Chiefs year (Wikipedia 1959; others 1953).

name: Mokwugo Okoye
summary: Radical nationalist and writer. A leader of the Zikist Movement, he became its secretary-general after the 1948 sedition trial and was jailed after a second sedition trial in 1950. He opposed Biafran secession, wrote Storms on the Niger, and in 1992 helped found the Movement for National Reformation with Anthony Enahoro.
notes: DOCUMENTED (opened: Oyeweso 2021, https://www.njh.com.ng/admin/img/paper/Vol. 29-1 final.pdf and https://blerf.org/index.php/biography/enahoro-chief-anthony/ ): economy -80 (Zikist leadership adopted revolutionary socialism in 1949; in 1954 he stood for nationalising the economy); global -70 (1954: strongly opposed importing foreign capital); identity +70 (lone voice against secession 1966-70, citing the nation's indivisibility); federalism +65 (co-founded the MNR in 1992 to restore true federalism under the 'original compact'); democracy +60 (1950 trial: wanted a world free to practice democracy; MNR/NADECO pressed for civil rule); corruption -30 (1954: asked the NCNC to investigate all allegations against party men, including ministers); social +50 (supported the formation of Women In Nigeria, 1983). The study says he was never a communist, so economy stays below -90. ESTIMATED: religion -45 (an agnostic who criticised the 'unholy alliance' of Government, Church and Big Business), security +30 (Zikist method was civil disobedience based on non-violent cooperation, an anti-colonial tactic, not a state security policy). ZERO-PLACEHOLDER: power. A 2023 Guardian column (https://guardian.ng/opinion/the-followership-has-failed-us-again-how-sad/ , opened) also quotes his book on tribalism obtruding its 'ugly snout'. Dates for Storms on the Niger vary by source (1960 to about 1965).

name: Dr Michael Okpara
summary: Medical doctor and NCNC politician who served as Premier of Eastern Nigeria from 1959 to 1966. He described his approach as 'pragmatic socialism' and prioritised an agricultural revolution, with state-run plantations and the farm settlement scheme he announced in 1961.

name: Senator Joseph Sarwuan Tarka
summary: Tiv politician from Benue who became president of the United Middle Belt Congress in 1957 and allied it with the Action Group. He advocated creating a Middle Belt state to empower minority groups. After 1966 he served as federal commissioner for Transport and then Communications under Gowon, until 1974, and was a senator from 1979.

name: Herbert Macaulay
summary: Lagos civil engineer and surveyor who became a leading opponent of British colonial rule. He organised the Nigerian National Democratic Party to contest the first elective Lagos seats under the 1922 constitution, and campaigned on land tenure and the rights of the Eleko of Lagos. In 1944 he helped launch the NCNC and became its president.

summary: Physician and political organiser who founded the Socialist Workers and Farmers Party of Nigeria in 1963, a Marxist-Leninist party politically close to the Soviet Union that was banned in 1966. name: General Murtala Mohammed
summary: Army general who ruled Nigeria from July 1975 until his assassination in February 1976. His government dismissed thousands of public officials, created seven new states, appointed panels on a new constitution and on relocating the capital to Abuja, set a civilian handover for 1979, and recognised the MPLA in Angola. He gave the 'Africa has come of age' speech at the OAU in January 1976.

category: military officer, politician, Biafran head of state

name: General Sani Abacha
summary: Army general and Head of State from 1993 until his death in 1998. He took power after the annulled 1993 election, banned political parties, convened a constitutional conference in 1994-95, announced a transition programme in 1995, and oversaw Vision 2010 and the Petroleum Trust Fund. His rule is associated with detentions of opponents and the 1995 execution of Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight others.

summary: Nigeria's first executive president (1979-83), elected on the National Party of Nigeria ticket after serving as a federal commissioner and minister. His government pursued a 'Food and Shelter' platform including the Green Revolution programme and housing estates, launched an Ethical Revolution in 1982, and expelled many undocumented West African migrants in 1983. Overthrown in a coup on 31 December 1983.

summary: Architect and Nigeria's Vice President from 1979 to 1983.
